- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- Model consistently over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecasted peak.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not continue falling; add upward bias of 0.5–1.5% to counteract.
- When sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment momentum, not just price history.
- For horizon > 15 days, model under-estimates true volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is uncertain or mixed.
